title.narrative: Emergency response in flood affected Kogi state of Nigeria

description.narrative: From 24th of August 2018, torrential rains caused serious flooding in 12 states in Nigeria. 250-500 mm total rain fall was recorded in one month starting from 24th of August till 23rd September and this caused severe damage to public and private infrastructure and wiped out people's livelihoods. 13000 houses partly and fully damaged in extremely affected 4 target states of Anambra, Delta, Kogi and Niger. 122650 hectares of agricultural land has been affected and standing crops have been destroyed leaving affected population with looming food security crises in coming weeks and months. (Source ACAPS Update 26th September) In the 12 states, flooding has impacted 826,403 people and out of the total affected population 176,299 people are forced to be displaced in 10 out of 12 states affected. Among the 12 states affected by flooding in Nigeria, 4 states (Niger, Kogi, Anambra and Delta) have been declared as National Disaster by Federal Government of Nigeria: The consortium (Christian Aid, CARE International and CAFOD ) is well positioned to intervene in those 4 states and are ready to do so. Based on the data collected from the field under the supervision of the National Emergency Management Agency, which coordinates humanitarian action, the total of affected people in these 4 states is nearly 489,087. This project aims to provide emergency assistance through unconditional cash to 3600 extremelly affected and vulnerable families of 3 severely affected (Anambra, Kogi and Delta) states. CAFOD will specifically intervene in four LGAs in Kogi state; Kogi, Lokoja, Bassa and Omala. We will reach 1204HH in the four LGAs by providing unconditional cash transfer to the target HHs. Other add on activities would include WASH sensitization, protection mainstreaming/CRM and community mobilization, advocacy visits to National Emergency Management Agency/State Emergency Management Agencies( NEMA/SEMA), the government agency responsible for emergency response in Nigeria
